status_vocabulary.verified: implemented, and exercised by the named tests (adversarial fixtures) and, where stated, by a real-data run
status_vocabulary.partial: implemented for part of the clause; the gap field says what is missing
status_vocabulary.not_implemented: no code; the gap field says what would be needed
status_vocabulary.not_acquired: the data are not in the environment; the gap field says why
status_vocabulary.unavailable_input: the clause needs an input that does not exist in this environment
status_vocabulary.blocked_external: only a person outside this session can satisfy it

requirements.clause: Inspect branches, instructions, READMEs, scripts, manifests, datasets and tests.
requirements.how: inventory/repository_audit.py lists branches, documents, scripts (compiled), manifests and the dataset lifecycle, runs the checks and recomputes the numbers quoted in the READMEs and the latest AUDIT_LOG entry (with a mutation self-test of the claim checker).

requirements.clause: Reuse and preserve NHGRI, Ensembl, 1000 Genomes and MaveDB assets; no restart, deletion, history rewrite or structural changes without necessity and approval.
requirements.how: inventory/audit_existing.py --check compares every tracked file under scrape/ with the baseline checksums; check_repo_policy.py checks sizes, file types and credentials. Nothing under scrape/ was changed in this phase, no history was rewritten (decision: no rewrite), and the MaveDB score tables stay on their own branch.

requirements.clause: Distinguish listed, acquired, verified, mapped and integrated.
requirements.how: reports.lifecycle derives the five statuses of every acquisition target from targets.json, the manifest, the validation report and the built index (a target is integrated only if the index holds a release of it, and mapped only if one of its evidence rows is mapped to a normalised entity); inventory/repository_audit.py derives the same stages for the repository audit, where a target is also mapped when a passing join test used it (the targets the index does not hold have no evidence rows to count).

requirements.clause: Prefer bulk releases, official APIs and integration tools to webpage scraping.
requirements.how: Every acquisition target records its URL, method and SHA-256 in acquisition/manifest.jsonl; the sources are bulk releases (ClinVar VCF and VCV XML, GWAS Catalog tables, Open Targets Parquet, gnomAD files, PGS Catalog files) or official API exports (ClinGen, CPIC, ClinPGx, PharmVar).

requirements.clause: GWAS Catalog associations and relevant full summary statistics.
requirements.how: The associations table and study metadata are acquired and integrated (GwasCatalogAdapter).
requirements.gap: Full summary statistics are not downloaded and have no adapter: 181,588 of the 232,202 studies in the acquired studies table list them (per-study files, mostly molecular-QTL sets; this environment has a few GB of free disk), and the relevant studies have not been chosen. Association-level evidence does not stand in for them.

requirements.clause: Open Targets Platform variants, studies, credible sets, fine-mapping and colocalisation.
requirements.how: Studies, credible sets (with posterior inclusion probabilities) and locus-to-gene scores are acquired and integrated; gene-level evidence (IMPC, essentiality, CRISPR screens, gene burden) is integrated separately. The variant table is acquired and is used as the allele and frequency source that settles the orientation of GWAS Catalog effect alleles (alleles.py).
requirements.gap: The colocalisation datasets (15.4 GiB) are not downloaded. The variant table's own annotations (7.9 million variants: consequences, predictor scores, population frequencies; 1.97 GB) are acquired and join-tested but no adapter writes them into the index, so the lifecycle report lists the target as not integrated.

requirements.clause: ClinVar full releases plus GRCh38 VCF.
requirements.how: The GRCh38 VCF and the weekly VCV XML release (converted to Parquet tables) are acquired and integrated: aggregate classifications, every submission (SCV), structural events and composite records (haplotypes, genotypes).

requirements.clause: ClinGen gene-disease, dosage and actionability curations.
requirements.how: Gene-disease validity, haploinsufficiency / triplosensitivity (gene and region curation lists, recurrent CNV regions), adult and paediatric actionability assertions and scoring, and the evidence-repository variant classifications are acquired and integrated at gene, region and variant level.

requirements.clause: MaveDB scores and mappings.
requirements.how: Score tables (native-coordinate and protein-level mappings), calibrated classes and assay metadata are integrated; protein-only mappings stay ambiguous unless the genomic allele is determined.

requirements.clause: ClinPGx/CPIC and PharmVar definitions.
requirements.how: CPIC allele definitions and guidelines, PharmVar haplotype definitions and ClinPGx clinical annotations are integrated as haplotype-, gene- and variant-level evidence.

requirements.clause: PGS Catalog harmonised GRCh38 scoring files.
requirements.how: Every score in the catalogue is registered with its metadata, performance and sample ancestry rows and the gates that apply; GRCh38 scoring files are acquired for a tiered subset and scored with chromosome-wise streaming.
requirements.gap: Scoring files are acquired for a subset of the catalogue; the rest are registered as listed_not_acquired and cannot be scored here.

requirements.clause: gnomAD frequencies and constraint, and versioned reference and transcript context.
requirements.how: Constraint, LoF curation, structural-variant and copy-number events, and frequencies at the MaveDB-mapped positions are integrated; the Ensembl 116 FASTA and GTF, MANE and the RefSeq assembly report are mirrored and used for normalisation and contig bridging.
requirements.gap: Whole-chromosome gnomAD VCFs are not downloaded (size); allele frequencies are indexed only at the positions covered by the acquired regional slices.

requirements.clause: Verify access, coverage, licences, versions, schemas and storage needs before downloads.
requirements.how: Each source record in catalogue/ carries probed access, licence, version and size evidence; acquisition/validate.py checks every target after download; the licence travels into source_release.

requirements.clause: Link immutable source records to normalised entities.
requirements.how: Every evidence row carries release_id, accession, locator and the SHA-256 of the raw record text. provenance.verify_index re-opens the acquired files, recomputes the digests of a deterministic sample of rows per release with one rule per source (vindex/resolvers.py), and checks release linkage and manifest agreement.
requirements.gap: The digests are recomputed for a sample of 500 rows per release, not for every row. Entity rows (genes, studies, regions, events, haplotypes) carry the release of their source but not a per-row digest.

requirements.clause: Deduplicate identities, retain evidence.
requirements.how: Variants have one normalised key; xref carries rsIDs and database identifiers; evidence ids are deterministic hashes, so a record seen twice is one row. One NCBI Gene id resolves to one gene whichever of its ClinVar symbols a record carries (GeneMap.learn_ncbi_symbols); an unresolvable gene keeps its own namespaced identifier. Ontology and database identifiers have one spelling, PREFIX:LOCAL (build.common.curie: Open Targets' MONDO_0005393, ClinVar's MONDO:MONDO:0010178 and Human_Phenotype_Ontology:HP:0001250 become MONDO:0005393, MONDO:0010178 and HP:0001250; ClinVar's 'OMIM: 612621' loses its space and the ClinGen actionability export's bare MONDO number gets its prefix; a name typed among the identifiers, as in one Open Targets study, leaves condition_ids and is kept in extra_json as condition_ids_not_identifiers), evaluation dates are ISO dates, an rsID is never given the alternate allele of another variant at its position (the Catalog's rows are unmapped, not attached to the neighbour), and every variant that an identifier, a link, a definition or a row names is an entity; reports.validate checks the spellings and the references on every build.

requirements.clause: Preserve unmapped records, contradictions, negative findings, uncertainty and lineage.
requirements.how: mapping_status mapped / ambiguous / unmapped / rejected with a reason; effect_assertion effect / no_effect / uncertain / conflicting / not_applicable; lineage_group on every row.

requirements.clause: Shared studies across databases are not independent replication.
requirements.how: Rows that descend from one study share a lineage_group: pmid:<PMID> across the GWAS Catalog, Open Targets, ClinPGx and MaveDB; clinvar:variation:<id> across the ClinVar aggregate, its submissions and the ClinGen expert-panel classification of that variation. The per-axis summary counts independent lineages, not rows, and reports.lineage_sharing lists the groups that more than one source writes.
requirements.gap: Two sources that describe one record under different keys are not linked: the CPIC guidelines and ClinPGx's annotations of them (their identifiers are different ClinPGx objects), and a ClinGen classification whose file row names no ClinVar variation id. Their rows count as independent.

requirements.clause: Separate variant-, haplotype-, gene-, region-, assay- and study-level evidence; do not assign a gene's actionability to every variant.
requirements.how: The level column and per-level subject ids; gene-level evidence reaches a sample only through gene_context, labelled gene_level_context_only, and never as variant evidence.

requirements.clause: Parallel evidence axes; no single composite score or automatic A-E hierarchy; priority lists are views over the complete catalogue.
requirements.how: Seven axes (clinical validity / actionability, empirical functional support, mechanistic confidence, effect magnitude / direction, association / replication, fine-mapping probability, applicability context). views.py selects with explicit rules and prints its ordering; no score is computed. The same rules also list the high-value variants of the catalogue itself, with no sample involved (make_views.py --catalogue).

requirements.clause: Retain effect alleles, beta/OR, units, uncertainty, p-values, sample metadata, inheritance, penetrance, germline/somatic context and review status when supplied.
requirements.how: Dedicated evidence columns (effect_allele, other_allele, beta, odds_ratio, score_unit, se, ci_low, ci_high, p_value, pip, eaf, sample_size, n_cases, ancestry, inheritance, penetrance, origin, review_status, review_stars, n_submitters); source fields without a column go to extra_json. A source's marker for no value (., NR, n/a) is not kept as a value, a signed beta carries a signed interval, and non-finite numbers, frequencies outside [0,1] and non-positive standard errors are not stored as measurements; reports.validate checks all of these on every build.

requirements.clause: Link variant assays and KO/CRISPR/dosage perturbations with model, tissue and dose context; distinguish gene null from the specific allele.
requirements.how: MaveDB assays are variant-level evidence on their own assay entities. Gene-level perturbation evidence is kept apart from them: mouse knockout phenotypes (IMPC; model system, background, zygosity), the CRISPR knockout, essentiality and tissue-dependency evidence that Open Targets integrates, ClinGen dosage sensitivity and gnomAD constraint. The columns model_system, perturbation, dose, tissue and cell_type hold the context.
requirements.gap: The CRISPR evidence in the index is the gene-level evidence Open Targets integrates. The BioGRID ORCS bulk screens are acquired but not integrated separately, and DepMap's own files are not acquired (access restricted); the DepMap-derived essentiality that Open Targets integrates is in the index. No evidence about a specific allele comes from a gene perturbation.

requirements.clause: Separate molecular effects from inferred physiological and clinical effects; missing study evidence is not evidence of no effect.
requirements.how: Molecular, functional and clinical claims sit on different axes and claim types. A variant with no row for an axis has no assertion on that axis; no_effect is only written for an explicit negative record, and the matcher reports NO_INDEX_RECORD / ABSENT_FROM_CALLSET instead of a negative.

requirements.clause: Use 30x GRCh38 SNP/indel, CNV and SV calls.
requirements.how: vcfio reads VCF / gVCF (small alleles, symbolic SV / CNV alleles, repeat genotypes, reference blocks) and wgs.run_sample matches a whole file one contig at a time, then once more for every record off the primary assembly.
requirements.gap: No personal 30x callset exists in this environment. The pipeline is verified on synthetic fixtures and on the public GIAB HG002 benchmark callset (not anyone's personal genome).

requirements.clause: Reuse established normalisation, PGx and PGS tools.
requirements.how: Normalisation is cross-checked against bcftools norm (random variants in the tests, and a whole-run comparison of calls and evidence matches); PGS scoring is cross-checked against plink2; star alleles come from the CPIC and PharmVar definitions.
requirements.gap: The star-allele caller is this repository's own implementation of the published definitions; structural genes (CYP2D6, HLA, KIR) need a dedicated caller (Cyrius, Aldy, StellarPGx, PharmCAT) whose result is supplied with --external-haplotypes. None is installed here. A cross-check of the star-allele calls against PharmCAT (bioconda pharmcat3 3.4.0, MPL-2.0) was prepared and not run: the environment's permission policy did not allow the downloaded tool to be executed, so the star-allele logic is verified against the published definitions by tests and known-locus checks, not against another caller.

requirements.clause: Validate assembly and REF alleles.
requirements.how: assembly_check compares the VCF header contigs with the reference (build guess from the chr1 length); AssemblyMismatch stops a run unless explicitly overridden; every REF allele is checked against the FASTA and a mismatch is rejected and listed.

requirements.clause: Preserve genotype, phase and quality when normalising and splitting multiallelics.
requirements.how: Each split allele carries its own dosage, ploidy, phase and phase set, GQ, DP, allele depth, QUAL and filter; QC flags are recorded, not applied silently.

requirements.clause: Match normalised CHROM:POS:REF:ALT, not rsIDs alone; preserve effect-allele orientation and reject unresolved strand mappings.
requirements.how: Matching is by key only. GWAS rows whose strand cannot be resolved (palindromic or multiallelic sites) are rejected with the reason; effect and other alleles are stored with the row, and each link from a call to a row states the effect allele and how many copies of it the sample carries (a row about the reference allele reaches the sample through its alternate call, so the copies are the reference copies of the genotype, not ploidy minus dosage). A site whose genotype is a verified reference (gVCF block or callable region) is linked to the rows whose effect allele is the reference allele of a single-nucleotide key (call_kind verified_reference; two copies on an autosome, none stated on X, Y and the mitochondrion, where the providers do not record the ploidy); every such site is counted in the run manifest by what the sample says about it, and a site the sample cannot answer for, or at which another allele is called, has no link. A record the reader refused (REF disagrees with the reference) is a record at its site, so reference is not verified there; crosscheck_bcftools.py --reference-sites recomputes the verified sites from the index, the callable-region BED and bcftools and compares them with the links.

requirements.clause: Protein-only assay mappings may remain ambiguous.
requirements.how: MaveDB protein-level variants are mapped to genomic alleles only when the codon change is determined; otherwise they are ambiguous rows that list the candidate alleles.

requirements.clause: Interval overlap alone is not an equivalent CNV/SV; assess event type, dosage, breakpoints and uncertainty.
requirements.how: match_sv requires compatible type, reciprocal overlap, breakpoint agreement within the stated uncertainty and, where the index states a copy number, the same dosage; near-misses are returned with the reason they were refused.

requirements.clause: Require suitable evidence for haplotypes, star alleles and repeat lengths.
requirements.how: match_hap resolves a diplotype only when every defining position has a confident genotype (phase or an unambiguous diplotype) and otherwise says which positions are missing; match_repeat classifies only repeat sizes reported by a repeat genotyper, and keeps every repeat genotype of the file (NO_INDEX_RECORD when the index has no locus or threshold for it).
requirements.gap: Repeat lengths are not estimated from short reads; without ExpansionHunter / TRGT output the repeat loci are reported as unresolved.

requirements.clause: Distinguish exact matches, verified reference calls, filtered/no-calls, absent-from-callset and unresolved loci.
requirements.how: Statuses EXACT_MATCH, FILTERED_CALL, NO_INDEX_RECORD for calls; VERIFIED_REFERENCE, NO_CALL, ABSENT_FROM_CALLSET, OTHER_ALLELE_AT_SITE, DELETED_BY_UPSTREAM, UNRESOLVED for indexed loci, each with its basis.

requirements.clause: Absence from a variant-only VCF never establishes reference genotype; resolve using gVCF/reference calls or targeted reads as needed.
requirements.how: Reference is established only by gVCF blocks or a declared callable-region mask (with the all-variants assumption recorded in the basis); otherwise the locus is ABSENT_FROM_CALLSET, NO_CALL or UNRESOLVED with the exact missing evidence. With aligned reads (match_wgs.py --reads) the small variants a callset leaves open are also asked of the reads (vindex/reads.py): the fragments that carry the reference, the indexed alternate or another sequence over a window are counted after stated filters (mapping and base quality, flagged duplicates, one count per fragment), and the locus gets a read state beside the matcher status, never over it, with whether that settles the open question (the presence of the indexed allele, not its copy number or phase). The absence of alternate fragments is read as reference only at depth and when no caveat applies (soft-clipped reads ending at the site, a deletion over it, disagreeing mates, low-mapping-quality reads that dominate or look like the alternate). Checked on synthetic alignments (indel placements an aligner can choose, filters, caveats, CRAM, assembly refusal; a mutation check of the module) and on public HG002 reads against the GIAB benchmark (1,200 benchmark alleles and 1,000 random absent ones, at 60x, 30x and 15x; validate_reads.py, reads_validation.json).
requirements.gap: No personal reads exist in this environment, so no personal locus has been settled by reads. The resolver tests the presence of the indexed allele; it is not a genotyper (no zygosity, copy number, phase or contamination model), it does not change the matcher status or the verified-reference links, it is tuned for short reads, and structural, copy-number and repeat-length loci are not asked of reads. Against the benchmark at 60x: 97.6% of 800 heterozygous and 97.5% of 400 homozygous benchmark alleles read as carried, 0 of 1,000 absent alleles read as carried, 16 of 1,187 claims at the benchmark alleles contradict it (a read haplotype that differs from the indexed allele because another variant lies beside it, or an insertion no read of the alignment shows); at 30x 96.1% and 96.8%, at 15x 87.0% and 94.8% (more abstentions). The benchmark covers its confident regions only, where reads are easier to place than elsewhere.

requirements.clause: Keep personal calls and results local and out of Git history and external services.
requirements.how: match_wgs.py and score_pgs.py refuse an output directory inside the tracked tree; .gitignore blocks VCF / BAM / CRAM / FASTQ files anywhere; matching is a local bulk join and never queries an external service per variant; check_repo_policy.py scans for personal-genome file types.

requirements.clause: Reusable master index.
requirements.how: build_index.py builds the Parquet index (13 tables, schema in SCHEMA.md) from the acquired sources into data/index, always from an empty directory, with per-table digests.

requirements.clause: Evidence-linked, prioritised WGS matches.
requirements.how: match_wgs.py writes small_calls, evidence_links, gene_context, sv_calls, haplotype_calls, repeat_calls, unresolved_loci, rejected_calls and a run manifest; make_views.py prepares the priority lists.

requirements.clause: Trait and pathway views.
requirements.how: views.trait_view groups matched evidence by the sources' condition identifiers (every one spelled PREFIX:LOCAL by the build) and views.trait_rollup rolls the traits up through the Open Targets disease and phenotype ontology table (ancestors and therapeutic areas; a trait in several areas is counted in each). An id the table does not hold is placed through the terms that list it as a cross-reference (a MedGen concept through the UMLS cross-reference, OMIM, MeSH, Orphanet; the prefix is part of the match) or that replace it when it is a retired term; the mapping is kept (cross_referenced: the terms, how, whether it is many-to-one, in which case the trait is counted in the areas of every term) and a cross-reference groups without asserting that two concepts are the same. pathway_view groups by Reactome gene-set membership; all three are annotation over the complete tables and none changes or combines evidence.
requirements.gap: Trait identifiers that no term of the Open Targets ontology table holds, lists as a cross-reference or replaces (MedGen concepts and OMIM ids the table does not list, retired EFO, MONDO and HP terms without a replacement, GeneReviews) are listed as not rolled up and stay as the sources wrote them: 203 of the 10,306 traits of the HG002 run (81 MedGen, 36 EFO, 28 HP, 27 OMIM, 21 MONDO, 4 Orphanet, 3 MeSH, 2 GeneReviews, 1 PATO); another 160 are placed through a cross-reference or a retired-term link (8 of them to more than one term), 9,943 through their own term. No other ontology mapping is made (a MedGen disease is not matched to a MONDO term by name).

requirements.clause: High-value unresolved loci with the exact missing evidence.
requirements.how: An index-centric pass over the high-value rules lists every indexed allele the sample cannot answer for, with status, reasons and the evidence that would settle it.

requirements.clause: Manifests, coverage statistics, change log, validation and gap report.
requirements.how: index_manifest.json and table_digests.json (build, with the digest of the code that built it), reports.coverage / validate / lifecycle / change_log / gap_report through make_reports.py (coverage includes the lineage groups shared between sources; validate includes value-level checks), run_manifest.json (per sample).

requirements.clause: Use full PGS models separately, checking allele dosage, missingness and ancestry/calibration before interpretation.
requirements.how: PGS scoring is a separate product: dosage from the genotype, missingness and weight coverage, ancestry compatibility and calibration gates; an interpretation is withheld when a gate fails. The result lists the gates.
requirements.gap: Ancestry is taken from a declared value, not inferred from the genotypes, and reference score distributions are not part of the repository, so calibrated percentiles are not produced.

requirements.clause: First verify a source -> index -> matcher slice with adversarial fixtures: equivalent alleles, nonmatches, ambiguous phase, REF mismatches, missing calls and unequal overlapping SVs.
requirements.how: Synthetic reference with engineered repeats, fixtures for every source format, and end-to-end tests of equivalent representations, REF mismatches, phase, no-calls, reference blocks and SVs with unequal overlap.

requirements.clause: Check provenance, preservation and idempotence; revalidate after source or schema changes.
requirements.how: verify_index.py (provenance, with a resolver for every source), audit_existing.py --check (preservation), table digests compared across two builds that ran in separate processes (idempotence; the manifest records the digest of the build code), crosscheck_bcftools.py (ClinVar rows and sample calls against bcftools), compare_runs.py (two matcher runs of one input with different hash seeds, table by table), verify_known_loci.py (facts established outside the index: an rsID's position, the direction of an association, a classification, a star allele's defining variant, a curated gene or region assertion), reports.change_log between builds and reports.validate after every build; gap_audit.py ties the index to the commit whose build modules have the digest its manifest records and the idempotence report to that digest.

requirements.clause: Execute available non-destructive work; mark unavailable inputs and unimplemented modules; report only verified work.
requirements.how: reports.MODULES states implemented / partial / unimplemented / not_acquired / unavailable_input for every module and the gap report prints it; STATUS.md is written from test and run results.

requirements.clause: Verify 'dc' privacy. Never commit personal genome files or sensitive third-party data. Private status does not waive licences.
requirements.how: inventory/check_repo_policy.py checks the live visibility of the repository and scans tracked files for personal-genome file types and credential patterns; licences are carried per release.
requirements.gap: The live check reports the repository as public. The session's proxy refuses repository-settings writes, so only the owner can make it private. No personal genome file or sensitive third-party data is tracked.

requirements.clause: Declare this phase complete only after defined requirements and an adversarial gap audit pass.
requirements.how: This table defines the requirements; requirements.json is checked by tests (paths, test modules, statuses, no orphan code or test); the executable gap audit (inventory/gap_audit.py, report in inventory/PHASE_AUDIT.md) attacks the work from outside: the map, the documentation, the audit-log numbers, the history for personal files, the built index (validation, provenance, idempotence, bcftools cross-checks) and the sample run (accounting, missing-evidence text).
